source_anchor: Roles and responsibilities across enrollment/proofing, authenticator management, and federation
notes: Cross-part provider role; exact responsibilities are distributed across the suite.
Evidence is collected and validated as part of proofing.
Resolution precedes validation/verification and distinguishes an identity in the relevant population/context.
Validation concerns authenticity/accuracy/validity of evidence and attributes.
Verification establishes that the applicant is the person associated with the validated evidence.
Composite process containing resolution, validation, and verification requirements.

source_anchor: Enrollment and post-proofing establishment of subscriber/account relationship
notes: Enrollment follows successful proofing and supports subsequent authenticator binding.

source_anchor: Enrollment record / subscriber account; Authenticator Event Management

source_anchor: Definitions and role usage throughout suite
notes: Contextual role after enrollment; avoid universal-class overcommitment.
IAL is the proofing assurance dimension and remains distinct from AAL/FAL.
Authenticator participates in authentication and has a managed lifecycle.
Authentication demonstrates control of bound authenticator(s) under AAL requirements.
AAL is the authentication assurance dimension; do not collapse into IAL/FAL.
Session is established/maintained after authentication and has independent lifecycle constraints.
Federation conveys authentication/attribute information across separately administered systems.
IdP is a federation role; Rev4 wallet model requires role-sensitive treatment.
RP consumes validated assertion and makes local decisions; role mapping already exists.
Intermediary federation role; effective assurance must respect chain semantics.
